subject: math
explanation:
Why Is Comparing Large Numbers Difficult?
Look at these numbers:
•

4,500,000

•

45,000,000

•

450,000,000

Many students make mistakes while counting zeros.
Now imagine scientists comparing:
•

Distance to planets

•

Number of stars

•

Size of bacteria

•

Speed of light

It becomes even harder.
This is why Standard Form becomes useful.

Example 1: Large Numbers
Compare:
3.2 × 108
and
5.7 × 107
First compare exponents:
8>7
Therefore:
3.2 × 108
is larger.
No calculation needed.

 Example 2: Same Exponent
Compare:
3.5 × 106
and
8.2 × 106
Exponents are same.
Now compare coefficients:
3.5 and 8.2
Since:
8.2 > 3.5
Therefore:
8.2 × 106
is larger.

Example 3: Very Small Numbers
Compare:
5 × 10−4
and
5 × 10−6
Remember:
10−4
is larger than:
10−6

 Therefore:
5 × 10−4
is larger.

Quick Comparison Rule
For Large Numbers
Bigger exponent = Bigger number

For Small Numbers
Exponent closer to zero = Bigger number
Example:
10−2
is bigger than:
10−5

sections.heading: 5. MISCONCEPTIONS
sections.content:
Misconception 1
Bigger coefficient always means bigger number.
Wrong.
Example:
9 × 105
is smaller than:
2 × 106
because exponent matters more.

Misconception 2
Bigger negative exponent means bigger number.
Wrong.
10−6
is smaller than:
10−3

Misconception 3
Standard form changes number value.
Wrong.
Only representation changes.

Misconception 4

 Scientific notation is only for scientists.
Wrong.
Used in:
•

computers

•

engineering

•

economics

•

medicine

•

astronomy

Q1

 Answer: A

and

Q5

 Answer: D

10−4
